A glovelike weapon studded with sharp spikes and edges across the knuckles and the back of the glove. Gladiators usually wear two, one on each hand (plural cesti). REQUIRES NO WEAPON PROFICIENCY -- it is simply a bonus to punching-type attacks and anyone may use cesti with no proficiency penalty, so Specialization with Cestus costs only one weapon proficiency slot. A character wearing cesti may still make a Grab maneuver with that hand, at -2 to hit and -2 to the attacker's Strength for holding on. Readily available from weaponsmiths in any culture with gladiatorial combat, but not exported; a foreign weaponsmith who has cesti described to him can make functional ones, but the first two cost twice the listed price. One-handed only. PHBR1 p.96. ONE-HANDED ONLY (PHBR1 pp.95, 119, marked '!'): intended for one-handed use and may not be used two-handed.

A gladius (short sword) of Exceptional quality per the weapon-quality rules in PHBR1's Character Creation chapter. Indistinguishable from an ordinary gladius except by testing the blade. Better-tempered metal, sharpened to a razor edge: +1 damage and a NON-MAGICAL +1 to hit over the normal gladius -- which does NOT confer the ability to hit monsters requiring magical weapons. DISADVANTAGE: after any day in which it has been fought with, even for one attack, someone with the Armorer or Weaponsmithing secondary skill, or the Blacksmithing, Armorer or Weaponsmithing nonweapon proficiency, must sharpen it for half an hour; otherwise it acts as an ordinary short sword, losing both bonuses, until it is sharpened. Exposure to high heat -- a forge, dragon's breath, lava -- ruins the temper PERMANENTLY, turning it into an ordinary short sword forever. Uses SHORT SWORD proficiency; specialization in one transfers to the other. Any weaponsmith in a gladiatorial culture with an ability check of 14 or better can make one. One-handed only. PHBR1 pp.95-96, 98, 119. WEAPON QUALITY, AND A DOUBLE-COUNT TRAP. PHBR1 pp.10-11 make Exceptional quality +1 to hit AND +1 to damage. THE +1 DAMAGE IS ALREADY IN THE DICE ABOVE -- this row is 1d6+1/1d8+1 against Sword, Short's 1d6/1d8 -- but the +1 TO HIT IS NOT, because core_wp.json has no field for it. A Drusus should therefore carry hitAdj 1 and dmgAdj 0 on the character's weapon card, NOT an Exceptional quality preset, or the damage is counted twice. The hit bonus is explicitly NON-MAGICAL and does not let the weapon strike creatures requiring magical weapons. A length of rope with a loop at the end; the wielder holds the slack in his off-hand, twirls the lasso in his other, and hurls the loop. ON A HIT THE ATTACKER MUST DECLARE WHAT HE IS TRYING TO ACCOMPLISH -- the book gives five uses. TRIP: a Called Shot to the legs; target makes a Dexterity check with Pull/Trip modifiers or falls. PIN ARMS: a Called Shot to the arms; target makes a Strength check with Pull/Trip modifiers or both arms are pinned as per the Pin maneuver, each additional lasso giving -4 to his Strength for struggling, and at Strength 0 he cannot escape. DISMOUNT A RIDER: no Called Shot needed, but both parties must make Strength rolls when the mount's movement reaches the end of the rope -- loser takes 1d2 (rope torn from hands) or 1d3 (yanked from the saddle); tie both. SNAG THE HEAD: a Called Shot to the head, 1d3 damage plus Strength bonus on the hit and 1 point plus Strength per round thereafter; if the wielder can hoist the victim into the air it becomes 1d4 STRANGULATION damage per round with no Strength bonus, and a strangling victim cannot shout or raise the alarm. Tying the rope to a stationary object wins the Strength contest automatically unless the rope breaks. Range is a function of the rope's length rather than a throw, so the book gives it S 1, M 2, L 3 with no fixed rate of fire. Two-handed only. PHBR1 pp.94-95, 98, 119. TWO-HANDED ONLY (PHBR1 pp.95, 119, marked '&'): intended for two-handed use only.

WEAPON QUALITY (PHBR1 pp.10-11) applies to every weapon in this file and is NOT a property of the weapon TYPE -- it belongs to the individual item, so it is carried on the character's weapon card via hitAdj/dmgAdj rather than here. Poor: -1 hit, -1 damage, breaks on a natural 1-5 to hit. Average: no modifier; the DM may optionally break it on a natural 1, never automatically. Fine: +1 to hit OR +1 damage, chosen by the smith, never both. Exceptional: +1 to hit AND +1 damage. Fine and Exceptional break only in remarkable circumstances. All of these bonuses are NON-MAGICAL. Enchantments are typically made on weapons of at least Fine quality. ONE-HANDED ONLY (PHBR1 p.93): can be wielded in one hand only.
TWO-HANDED ONLY (PHBR1 p.93): cannot be wielded in one hand. The sling is listed here because one hand loads it and the other throws.
